title: WHEN WE MAKE PROMISES TO GOD

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
The LORD said to Moses, "Speak to the Israelites and say to them: 'If
anyone makes a special vow to dedicate a person to the LORD by giving
the equivalent value'" - Lev 27:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The book of Leviticus ends on an unexpected note. After all the laws
about sacrifice, holiness and festivals, the final chapter is about
vows — the voluntary promises people made to God out of love and
gratitude.

Nobody was required to make these vows. They arose spontaneously.
Someone experienced God's kindness — a recovery, a rescue, a prayer
answered — and in their overflowing thankfulness they said, "Lord, I
want to give You something in return."

Dear friend, there is something touching about God devoting a whole
chapter to these free promises. He takes seriously what we offer Him
freely. Our spontaneous devotion matters to Him.

But notice also the direction the chapter will take. God cares very
much about whether we keep what we promise. It is easy to make grand
vows in an emotional moment and quietly forget them once life settles.

Solomon warned, when you make a vow to God, do not delay to fulfil it,
for He has no pleasure in fools; fulfil your vow (Eccl 5:4). Jesus
taught that our yes should simply mean yes (Matt 5:37).

Have you made promises to God that you have let slip? A commitment made
in a hospital corridor, a pledge whispered in a crisis? God remembers
them, and He invites you to take them seriously again.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I made promises to God that I have quietly abandoned?
2. Do my words to God carry the weight they should?
3. What spontaneous devotion could I offer God out of gratitude?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that You take my freely given devotion seriously. Help
me keep the promises I make to You and to give You my gratitude honestly.
Amen.
